terms.gloss: in reversed order, the wrong way round
evidence: Plin. NH 2.24: laevus calceus praeposterē inductus (Lewis & Short s.v. praeposterus)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “in a reversed order, irregularly”. Pliny has it of a shoe put on the wrong foot; of clothes put on back to front, praeposterē induere (our phrase).

phrases.english: to put on back to front
